sintomas.plan_accion: Elevated lead alone is often related to sleeve bearings Re sample to confirm readings Confirm if fluid hours have been extended and justify elevated readings Inspect filters, plugs and screens for any signs of metal or debris Inspect breathers, coupler, clamps, seals for condition to limit dirt ingestion Confirm correct oil viscosity for application

sintomas.sintoma: Viscosity does not meet expected limits
sintomas.plan_accion: Confirm if oil grade was changed. Fuel contamination can cause lower viscosity. Use CAT ET to confirm injector operation. Trouble shoot HPFP for possible source of fuel contamination. Run priming fuel pump with magnetic plug from HPFP removed.

Elevated sodium is often related to coolant contamination. Supporting indicators are K, Si. Resample to confirm readings. Monitor engine oil and coolant levels. Inspect expansion tank for signs of oil in the coolant. Inspect for external leaks at water pumps and cylinder block. Possible integral gasket failure, inspect for visible change in the exhaust. Less common are liner seals or cracks.
Inspect: -Filter seal / condition -tension of clamps -condition of coupler / elbow -condition of pipe

Iron can be sourced to Liners, crankshaft, camshaft. Look for the root cause of elevated iron. New component. Recent repairs. contamination causing third body abrasion. Supporting wear metals that may indicate component failure. Cut open and inspect filter.

Elevated copper can be related to wear of brass components. Supporting indicators are Pb, Sn, Ni. Brass components can be a crank or cam thrust washers, Cooler Core, Severe sleeve bearing wear (precursor Pb, Sn). Copper on its own if often related to cooler leaching. Confirm if there were a change in oil type or contaminants (IE: coolant, Oxidation) causing cooler core leaching which is not related to wear. Inspect filters and plugs for signs of contaminants in the system causing third body abrasion (dirt, soot, metals, etc).

Check present alerts Perform hot plate tests to discard or confirm contamination take against sample Check vents for possible condensation Check washing process and possible leaks Check water pump status Check coolers Replace oil and filters
Check oil levels Check reinforcement work pressures

Field tests such as hot plate must be carried out to determine contamination of the refrigerant to the lubrication system. Inspect oil level, engine vent for condensation. Check for leaks by UF and by coolant pump acknowledgment. If the condition is maintained, the engine oil cooler should be evaluated. After the repair, oil and filter changes must be made. Take lubrication and temperature pressures. Schedule a new sample for the next 50 hours to monitor trends.

Perform internal inspection with borescope to assess the level of wear to determine the change of component Perform mitigation plan (oil change) as long as the component is reprogrammed for component change Keep on monitoring until the component replacement
Perform inspection of particulate routines Check lubrication pressures Take new sample for trend control

Verify the accuracy of service to determine the action plan (do not consider engines with oil hours extension) Verify if there is a previous chiller change or an engine change, this condition is considered normal (leaching process) Complement routine analysis Particulate as appropriate (filters, grilles and patch test) Depending on the engine hours, check and subsequent regulation of motor valves should only be carried out if they are out of range. Take lubrication pressures of pressure and operating temperature. new sample for trend control

Perform particulate routine evaluations (patch test, filter cut and grid inspection) Depending on the engine hours, check and subsequent regulation of motor valves should be carried out only those that are out of range Perform inspection for possible leakage of oil (remove) Take oil pressures and take new oil sample for trend control

Check possible filling with lower viscosity oil Check oil level and investigate for possible transfer Check particulate in magnetic plug, filters and oil draining process Check lubrication pressures Consider changing oil and keep on constant monitoring

Take 2 samples to perform field tests with viscometer and another to send to the laboratory. Take lubrication pressures and pressure trend analysis. Perform evaluation of diagnostic codes of injectors and visually check those that present problems to evaluate possible leaks at the top. (Trouble coils) Perform cylinder cutting Perform high pump magnetic plug inspection Check transfer pump status Pressurize fuel system to determine possible leaks of injector ring seals Use diagnostic reference information REHS3007

Field tests such as hot plate must be carried out to determine contamination of the refrigerant to the lubrication system. Inspect oil level, engine vent for condensation. Check leaks by refrigerant pump acknowledgment. Evaluate engine oil cooler. After the repair, oil and filter changes must be made. Take lubrication and temperature pressures. Schedule a new sample for the next 50 hours to monitor trends

Verify the accuracy of service to determine the action plan (do not consider engines with oil hours extension) Perform event control by air filter saturations and low power arrests to complement analysis. Complement analysis of particulate routines as appropriate (filters, grilles and patch test) According to the engine hours a check and subsequent regulation of motor valves should be carried out only those that are out of range Take lubrication pressures in a manometric way and temperature of operation Take a new sample for trend control

Analyze particulate in filters, patch test and grilles Inspect sweeping pump sprocket by sight glass cover for possible wear or pump looseness Take lubrication pressures Evaluate a check and regulate valves only if the condition and hours of the engine so Amerita Take new oil sample for monitoring
Check if there is a change of previous cooler or a change of engine, this condition is considered normal (leaching process) Take new sample for trend control Perform patch test and / or filter cut

Field tests such as hot plate must be carried out to determine contamination of the refrigerant to the lubrication system. Inspect oil level, engine vent for condensation. Check for leaks by UF and by coolant pump acknowledgment. If the condition is maintained, the engine oil cooler should be evaluated. After the repair, oil and filter changes must be made. Take lubrication and temperature pressures. Schedule a new sample for the next 50 hours to monitor trends.

The events appearing are “Fuel Control Valve: Special Instruction” (263-18-14) “SAE J1939 Data Link #2” (263-2348-9). "Fuel Control Valve: Abnormal Update Rate" (36-18-9) Are events are associated with the FCV communication.

The increasing number of 2854 - 9 events indicate that the TCM. (E Stat) cannot communicate with the engine ECM. Perform circuit testing of the CAN Datalink. ( SiS M0069788-02) *Note* A Fluke 123 meter can be a helpful tool for Datalink troubleshooting.

Check magnetic plugs for debris , replace HPCR fuel pump as soon as possible. The event 1684-12 is registered and due to the failure mode (FMI12) there are internal problems of the high pump, this must be replaced as soon as possible, since it will have an imminent failure (As it indicates internal bulletin TIBU2015067)
Perform Fuel system verification.Replace fuel injectors that remain - 07 codes at next service interval.

Once the resonator event (1684-12) has been presented, the HPFP pump must be checked and the equipment stopped immediately Replace the high fuel pump Inspect the outgoing pump magnetic plug to identify if there is any type of particulate and perform the following steps: 1- If the magnetic plug of the removed pump shows excessive contamination, it indicates that the failure of the pump did NOT generate contamination for the fuel system, since the fault is in the lower part of the pump. The equipment can be sent to operation without additional interventions. 2- If the magnetic plug of the pump does NOT have excessive contamination, the “in-line high-pressure fuel filter element” (also known as “edge filter” or “edge filter”) must be replaced. Once the edge filter is replaced, "Injector Bypass Fuel Flow - Test" must be performed, available in SIS MS075103

Use ET tool to check active codes, download product status and ECM replacement file. With the ECM replacement file perform the analysis of the VOT chart to define the injectors with problems (only for contracts that use the VOT analyzes) With the report of the product status or background vims check when the first injector events were generated with FMI-07. Schedule injector replacement before exceeding 1,500 hours of operation since the first FMI-07 event was generated.
